frozen: Authored 18-Sep from the official manual chunk text and corrected the same day, BEFORE the first run and before any fix was tested. Every required phrase and page was checked against that text. These questions are held out of tuning: if a result later guides a fix, the affected case is relabelled a development case in the report.
changes_in_this_version: fresh-wo-named-1: the forbidden item is no longer the string 'unplanned w.o'. What fails is an INSTRUCTION to create an unplanned work order as the way to do this. A one-line note that other methods exist is allowed, as prompt v5 permits.
fresh-incident-1: now also checks the view and edit actions on a notification, not only the filtering.
fresh-technical-1: now also checks the Fleet and Add Group filters alongside Vessel, Due Status and Clear.
fresh-audit-1: 'next' replaced by the destination it leads to (the Observation page), so the check cannot be satisfied by an unrelated use of the word 'next'.
fresh-safety-1: now requires both sides of the contrast (all reports versus only those awaiting an office response).
fresh-crewing-1: 'column' replaced by the column-header filter behaviour, and the named filter fields added.
fresh-moc-alt-1: all three creation routes must be present, not merely the words.
fresh-wo-broad-1: adds the attribution rule — automatic generation or the office Generate Now action may only appear if attributed to the draft code-derived guidance.
fresh-ctx-1: adds the module expectation (Safety) so the context test is scored, not just the topic words.
every case: added score_by, which states that meaning, conditions and source support decide the verdict; required phrases are an aid to the reader, never the verdict on their own.
scoring_rule: A case passes a run when: the steps and conditions are right; Office/Ship (Office/Vessel) applicability is right; every substantive claim is supported by an excerpt actually supplied in that run; the answer's own source references point at supporting sections; and any statement comparing sources is accurate. Literal phrase matching never decides a verdict on its own — markdown emphasis, tense, plurals and inserted words are not defects.

cases.question: After I create an inspection record in Audit History, what do the Save, Upload and Next buttons do, and which fields must I complete?
cases.score_by: Must state: all mandatory fields marked with an asterisk are completed; Save stores the inspection details; Upload attaches the required supporting documents; Next moves on to the Observation page (the destination matters, not the word 'next').
cases.evidence: An inspection record will be created. Complete all mandatory fields marked with (*). Click Save to save the inspection details. Click Upload to attach the required supporting documents. Click Next to proceed to the Observation page and enter the observation details, as applicable.

cases.file: Incident - Fleet Notification User Manual_Vessel_ R0_20.03.2026.pdf
cases.question: As a vessel user, how do I filter the fleet notifications shared by the office, and what can I do with a notification from that list?
cases.score_by: Two parts, both required. Filtering: open Filters, choose a Period or search by title, then Apply to filter or Clear to reset. Actions: the action icons let the user VIEW or EDIT the selected notification. An answer that covers only the filtering half is partial.
cases.evidence: The Fleet Notification screen displays notifications shared by the Office. Click Filters to access filtering options. Select the required Period or search using the title field. Click Apply to filter the records or Clear to reset. Use the action icons to view or edit the selected notification.

cases.question: In Master Review, what is the difference between the All tab and the Response Pending tab?
cases.score_by: Both sides of the contrast are required: All shows all reports; Response Pending shows only those awaiting an office response. Naming one side only is partial.
cases.evidence: Toggle between the All and Response Pending tabs to view either all reports or only those awaiting an office response.

cases.question: How do I filter candidate records in Crewing, and is there a way to filter an individual column?
cases.score_by: Must state: click Filter; refine with the search field and the dropdown filters (at least two of Rank Applied, Vessel Type, Nationality, Status, Manning Agent); Apply to filter or Clear to reset; AND that a filter icon in each column header allows column-wise filtering (the second half of the question).
cases.evidence: Click on the 'Filter' button. Use the search field along with filters such as Rank Applied, Vessel Type, Nationality, Status, and Manning Agent to filter candidate data. Click 'Apply' to filter the results or 'Clear' to reset the selection. Users can also click the filter icon in each column header of the table.

cases.file: Technical - Cert. & Surveys User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026.pdf
cases.question: In the Office Certificates screen, which filters can I use to narrow the certificate records, and how do I reset them?
cases.score_by: All four documented filters are required — Vessel (dropdown, for vessel-specific records), Fleet, Add Group and Due Status — plus Clear to reset. Listing only Vessel and Due Status is partial.
cases.evidence: Click on the 'Filter' button. Select the required vessel from the 'Vessel' dropdown to view vessel-specific certificate records. Use the 'Fleet', 'Add Group', and 'Due Status' filters to refine and view the displayed records based on the selected fleet, group, or certificate due status (e.g., All, Overdue, Upcoming Due). Click the 'Clear' button to reset all applied filters.

cases.question: What are the ways to start a new MoC from the office?
cases.section: 4. How to create a new MoC
cases.score_by: All three documented routes are required: + New MoC on the Dashboard page; + New MoC at the top right of the MoC Log; New MoC from the menu. Presenting one route as the only way is a defect.
cases.evidence: A new MoC can be created using any of the following methods: click '+ New MoC' on the Dashboard page; navigate to MoC Log and select '+ New MoC' on the top right corner; select New MoC from the menu.

cases.file: Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026.pdf
cases.question: What are the different ways a work order can come into existence in PMS?
cases.section: Components 'Generate WO' (p.18) and 1.1.5.2 How to create an unplanned work order (p.29)
cases.score_by: Both manual routes are required: the Components screen 'Generate WO' for a selected component (choose a reason), and '+ Unplanned W.O' on the Work Orders screen. Attribution rule: automatic ship-side generation and the office 'Generate Now' action appear ONLY in the draft code-derived guidance, so if the answer mentions either it must say that this comes from draft guidance rather than the manuals. Presenting unplanned creation as the only way is a defect.
cases.evidence: The official manuals describe TWO creation paths: (a) Components screen — 'The user can click the Generate WO button to create a WO manually for the selected component', then choose a reason (Office p.18; Vessel p.16); (b) Work Orders screen — '+ Unplanned W.O' (Office p.29, Vessel p.24). The manuals do NOT describe automatic daily generation or the office 'Generate Now' bulk action: 0 manual chunks contain 'Generate Now', 'job due' or 'daily scan'.

cases.file: Technical - PMS User Manual For Office_Sail Admin_R2_08.06.2026.pdf
cases.question: From the Components screen, how do I raise a work order for one job on a component?
cases.score_by: The procedure given must be the named one: select the component, click Generate WO, choose a reason from the listed options, and the work order is generated. DEFECT = instructing the user to create an unplanned work order instead, or presenting the unplanned route as the way to do this. ALLOWED = a brief closing note that other methods exist, which prompt v5 permits; merely mentioning '+ Unplanned W.O' as an alternative is not a failure.
cases.evidence: The user can click the 'Generate WO' button to create a WO manually for the selected component. The Generate Work Order pop-up appears; choose the appropriate reason for generating the work order from the listed options, and the Work Order will be generated. (Office p.18, Vessel p.16.)

cases.question: How do I record the minutes of a safety meeting?
cases.score_by: Scored on two things: the module chosen must be Safety (the originating module sent by the widget is technical and must not drag the question there), and the answer must come from the Safety Meeting manual — minutes are entered in Part B of the safety meeting form, with unresolved actions from the previous meeting shown, + Add Action to add actions, and Save.
cases.evidence: Asked with the originating module set to technical (the widget always sends the screen the user is on). The topic is Safety. Expected: the question routes to Safety and the answer comes from the Safety Meeting manual.
